text: Using HTTPS is the first step to protecting a website, as it encrypts data between the user and the server. However, security goes far beyond that. Proper authentication ensures that only authorized users can access sensitive areas, often through strong passwords or multi-factor authentication. Input validation is equally critical; never trust user-supplied data, as unchecked forms can lead to SQL injection or cross-site scripting (XSS), two of the most common vulnerabilities. Developers must also stay alert to other threats like broken access control or outdated software. Regularly testing the site for weaknesses, updating dependencies, and following security best practices are essential habits for building a safe, reliable web application.
